COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS

Pappu Ram .........Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ......Respondent

Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Applicant has moved this bail application in FIR
No.0279 of 2025 dated 05.06.2025 under Sections 351(3)
and 65(1) of B.N.S. 2023 and Section 3(b)/4 of POCSO Act,
2012, registered at Police Station-Rishikesh, District-Dehradun.
4. Facts of the case according to the FIR are that on
05.06.2025, in Mayakund Bengali Basti, Rishikesh,
approximately 7-year-old Ritu was lured into his room by
Sajjan Ram while on her way to collect stitched clothes from
a nearby shop. The accused showed her an obscene video,
inappropriately touched her private part, and threatened to
kill her and her parents if she disclosed the incident, after
which the victim managed to escape and reported the
occurrence to her mother, Smt. Anita Devi, who
subsequently filed a police complaint at Police Station
Kotwali Rishikesh.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the
applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the
present case due to false and frivolous allegations that do
not disclose any prima facie offence under Sections 65(1)
and 351(3) of the B.N.S. and under Section 3/4 of POCSO
Act, 2012.

2
6. It is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for
the applicant that initially the allegations made in the FIR
were made by victim against Sajjan Kumar but at the
concluding lines of the FIR it was submitted that action be
taken against Pappu Ram.
7. It is further submitted that the applicant has no prior
criminal history and is languishing in jail since 06.06.2025,
and on the grounds of his false implication and clean
antecedents, he is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
8. The learned counsel for the State vehemently opposes
the bail application, submitting that the allegations
disclosed in the FIR reveal a grave and heinous offense
committed against an approximately 7-year-old minor
victim, wherein the applicant lured her into his room,
subjected her to obscene content and sexual assault, and
intimidated her with threats to kill her and her parents.
Given the severity of the crime, the direct involvement of the
applicant as established by the FIR and victim's statement,
and the gravity of the accusations, the applicant is not
entitled to be released on bail.
9. Having considered the rival submissions of the parties,
perused the material available on record, this Court finds
that FIR attributes the alleged acts to one Sajjan Ram
whereas in concluding portion seeks legal action against the
present applicant Pappu Ram. Furthermore this Court finds
that although the statement of the victim contains the name
of the applicant, the cross examination of victim's mother
brings out certain circumstances surrounding his
implication, particularly in relation to presence of Sajjan
Singh and his family at a function. Such circumstances at

3
this stage do not sufficiently establish the applicant
involvement in the alleged incident.
10. Considering the aforesaid discrepancy that the
applicant has no criminal history and in judicial custody
since 06.06.2025, this Court is of the view that further
incarceration of the applicant is not warranted, therefore,
this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be
enlarged on bail.
11. Accordingly bail application of applicant-Pappu Ram is
allowed. Let applicant be released on bail, on his executing a
personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of
the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
